policy: Every failure, however small, is captured here BEFORE any recovery attempt. Never blindly repeat a failed command. Never lose completed outputs.

entry_schema.error_text: exact stderr / exception text, truncated only with an explicit marker
entry_schema.classification: one of: MISSING_DEPENDENCY | BAD_INPUT | RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED | TIMEOUT | PERMISSION | LOGIC_ERROR | DATA_CORRUPTION | NETWORK | TOOL_ABSENT | UNKNOWN
entry_schema.impact: what is now unusable, if anything
entry_schema.recovery_attempted: what was tried next (must differ from the failed command)

errors.error_text: jq -e . -> JSON CORRUPT. Line 215 became: "gauge": "31 to 22 to 14 to 6", She goes outside, ... The old_text pattern spanned into the adjacent "action" field and the new_text dropped the '"action": "The remaining stair gives way entirely.' prefix, leaving a dangling string literal.
errors.probable_cause: Fuzzy-match edit whose old_text crossed a JSON field boundary; replacement text did not re-emit the truncated field opener.
errors.impact: 01_DEVELOPMENT/MASTER_FILM_BRIEF.json unparseable. No checkpoint had been taken, so no committed artefact was affected.
errors.preserved_outputs: All other files untouched. The 11 required JSON keys and all arithmetic checks had already passed against the pre-corruption content.
errors.recovery_attempted: Rewrote line 215 in place with python (byte-exact, no fuzzy matching), then re-ran jq and the full arithmetic check. Future edits to this file use python or full-file rewrites, never cross-field fuzzy matches.

errors.error_text: turn_budget.costs rows 4-6 attributed costs to the wrong scenes. Row 'B06 Storm crossing, the pole is lost' cost=18 -> 40, but the pole is lost in SC05 (B05) and the 18-turn cost is the tower door in SC06. Row 'B07 Forcing the sealed tower door' cost=9 -> 31 was actually the stair giving way. Row 'B08 The stair gives way' cost=9 -> 22 was actually SC07 exposure. Costs and the 92->1 gauge chain were correct throughout; only the labels were wrong.
errors.probable_cause: T01 wrote the turn_budget as a flat list of beats (B03-B10) while story_beats used scene ids (SC03-SC08). The two numbering schemes drifted apart and were never cross-checked, so a stage-01 deliverable was marked VERIFIED with misattributed costs.
errors.impact: None downstream - caught at T02 before any scene breakdown was authored. Had it shipped, the continuity ledger would have credited the tower door's 18 turns to a storm crossing.
errors.preserved_outputs: All of stage 01: MASTER_FILM_BRIEF.md, MASTER_FILM_BRIEF.json, RESEARCH.md. Costs, gauge chain, scene plan, runtime and retention cadence all untouched.
errors.recovery_attempted: Rewrote the labels in both the JSON and the MD, added an explicit 'scene' field to every turn_budget row so the mapping is machine-checkable, and added a generator assertion that per-scene gauge deltas equal the budget rows for that scene. Verified costs and gauge chain were byte-identical before and after.
